Response readers share the existing owned preflight signal; scoped counter JSON also retains the combined eight-second RPC timeout, without a fresh body timer

Abort, overflow and read failure cancel and immediately release the reader even if the source cancellation promise never settles; malformed JSON, invalid UTF-8 and read errors expose fixed messages without payloads
Rejected HTTP response bodies are disposed for opted-in calls; existing gate decisions, limits, hashes, windows and no-signal contracts are retained

Six added actual helper groups cover exact boundary/split UTF-8, advertised/cumulative overflow, stalled source cancellation, partial-read abort, malformed/encoding/stream failures, all three helper limits and no-signal compatibility
Existing late-JSON cancellation tests now use real partial Response streams rather than deferred json stubs
Exact hosted 21 Exams/12 focused-entry/3 public-packs/7 scoped-read/14 generation-entry groups and six denials for each speech route pass

limits: Controlled byte/stream/error/cancellation tests do not establish real Supabase payload distributions, hosted overflow/preflight expiry or adapter buffering behavior. Existing auth parse failures retain their prior route handling; not every failure is HTTP 503.
Hosted speech checks send inadmissible input only. No positive provider/catalog/audio/microphone/billing/consent/browser or physical-device action occurred.
New bounds require the optional scoped signal. Other callers retain existing response.json behavior; this is not an app-wide JSON/network audit. Public catalog admission remains open.
Input/admission/provider deadlines remain separate, not one total delivery deadline. Cancellation cannot undo accepted counters/provider work or prove billing rollback/exactly-once execution.

Broader helper/endpoint/cache/diagnostics/device inventory, true SDK expiry/process restart/offline acceptance, uncertain writes/concurrency/legacy certificates and all human/content/calibration/equivalence/reviewer/pilot/catalog/retention/deletion/scheduler/platform gates remain open.
